title: x402 settlement census — one ROUND
description: One buyer's-eye round: every host in a fixed population paid once, at one moment, by a wallet the publisher controls, with the outcome of each purchase recorded. A round is the unit of the time series; two rounds make a delta (x402-census-delta-v1.json). Produced only by scripts/grants/x402_census_round.py from the round's own committed rows — every number here is derived, and `--check` recomputes the whole document and fails on a single changed byte. This document is measurement, not certification: it grades nothing, ranks nothing and recommends nothing, and REFUSED is not evidence of bad faith. No state above UNMEASURED is written at any level of this surface; per-host state belongs to the OIDC signer at n>=30 paid observations and lives on the card-v0 leaves, not here.

round_id.description: The UTC date the round was purchased. Rounds sort by this id and by nothing else.

mode.description: SETTLE means a signed payment was actually sent. A DRY-only pass is not a round: it records terms, not deliveries.

as_of.description: The LAST observed_at in the rows — never the time the file was written. A producer that stamps now() reports a change on every rebuild and tells a reader nothing.

window.description: first and last observed_at. A round takes minutes, not an instant, and says so.

network.description: CAIP-2 chain id of the settlement network.

population.description: hosts_sha256 is sha256 over the sorted newline-joined host list: two rounds with the same digest probed literally the same population, which is what makes a delta a time series rather than two unrelated samples.

caps.description: Hard spend caps in force for the round. These are OUR costs, not a price list: nothing this estate sells appears anywhere on this surface.

payer.description: The throwaway wallet the purchases came from. Every unit is a cost; no row here is revenue, and our own hosts are excluded from the population so no row can be a self-settlement.

rows.description: Path, sha256 and row count of each pass. The sha256 is the anchor: change one byte of the rows and every derived number in this file stops recomputing.

outcome.description: DELIVERED paid and answered with the advertised type; REFUSED paid and answered 402/4xx again; MISMATCH paid and answered 2xx with the wrong body; NO_CHALLENGE stopped returning a parseable 402 before anything was sent.

paid_rows.description: Rows where a signed payment was actually sent: DELIVERED + REFUSED + MISMATCH. This, not the delivered count, is what an observation accrues on — a series that counts only successes is not a measurement.

settlement_receipts.description: Whether the host returned a settlement reference of its own. `none` is common and is not an accusation.

take_and_refuse.description: Hosts that reported a settlement transaction in their own PAYMENT-RESPONSE and refused the retried request anyway. The definition travels with the number so nobody has to guess what was counted, and each row carries the tx hash so a reader checks the chain instead of trusting us.

pay_to.description: Concentration of the addresses the challenges name. A fact about the doors, not about any operator.

dry_vs_settle.description: The DRY pass runs minutes before the paid pass over the same hosts, so a door that moved its terms between the two is visible without waiting a week.

caveats.description: Carried in the artefact, never left to a covering note. At minimum: REFUSED is not proof of bad faith, and one purchase at one moment is not a pattern.

reproduce.description: The exact command a stranger runs to recompute this file.
